messages:
Priya (support): Heads up — customer ZetaCorp reports p95/p99 spikes for Dedicated pools since last night. They see occasional 10-20s tails during bursts. Opening thread with logs and sample request IDs.
Kevin (oncall): ack, adding to oncall. Any correlation with scale events?
Priya (support): Their timeline shows spike coinciding with autoscale events. Example request IDs: req-9ab, req-9ac. Support attached a short trace showing 'attach: waiting for pool' and then a long 'gpu-warmup' step.
Noah (eng-runtime): posting quick metrics: p95 increased from 400ms -> 1.8s, p99 from 1.2s -> 8s during the window. CPU on warmers looked fine, but attach time distribution has a fat tail at ~12s.
Olivia (eng-sre): any quota throttles from cloud side? I'm seeing provisioning start times consistent with VM boot ~6-9s, but our runtime warmup (load model, init kernels, jit) adds variable 4-10s depending on model and quantization. Combined that's ~10-18s worst-case.
maria (product): ZetaCorp is using a latency-sensitive route with model pinned to gpt-oz-large, min_pool_size=0, bursty traffic. They expect p95 < 1s.
Kevin (oncall): can we reproduce quickly? Priya, can you drop a repro script that mimics their pattern (short burst small requests, then idle)?
Priya (support): Posted repro script in thread: ```bash
# repro: 50 rps for 30s, then idle 5m, repeat 3x
for i in {1..3}; do seq 1 150 | xargs -n1 -P50 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/run -d '{"model":"gpt-oz-large","input":"hi"}'; sleep 300; done
```
Noah (eng-runtime): running locally against staging pool now. Observed attach latency median 650ms, p95 ~2.3s when pool is cold. Cold GPU init seems to be the variable.
Olivia (eng-sre): logs: svc-provisioner shows `scale_up: request queued (reason=burst)` followed by `cloud: start-instance` then `attach-agent: handshake` then `runtime: load-model`. Handshake time sometimes times out and we retry, adding ~3s. I see some backoff config using fixed 2s retry that causes synchronized retries across many attaches => thundering herd.
Kevin (oncall): that explains cascade. If many requests hit min_pool_size=0 pools, they all trigger attach at same time and our fixed retry aligns. We should randomize backoff and stagger warmups.
Noah (eng-runtime): proposed quick mitigations: 1) change attach retry to jittered exponential backoff (immediate PR), 2) add fast-path fallback to a lower-cost warmed replica (model-compat variant) when attach > 2s, 3) increase default `min_pool_size` for latency-sensitive routes or add a `warmup_policy`.
Priya (support): customer asked for immediate mitigation — can we do a config toggle for them to pin a small warm pool?
Olivia (eng-sre): yes, we can set min_reserved=1 on their dedicated pool. That will avoid cold starts for single-instance bursts. Coordination required with billing/ops to ensure capacity is available.
maria (product): also note risk: forcing min_reserved raises cost. Offer as temporary quickfix while we push runtime changes.
Kevin (oncall): runtime changes first — Noah, please drop a small patch for jittered backoff and reduce handshake timeout for early failover. We can hotfix to staging and roll to prod with canary.
Noah (eng-runtime): will open PR: change `attach_retry` from `fixed 2s x3` to `exp_backoff(initial=200ms, max=3s, jitter=0.5)` and handshake timeout from 5s -> 3s. Test plan: run repro against canary for 2 hours and measure p95/p99.
Olivia (eng-sre): ops mitigation: I'll allocate a spare GPU in region-us-west-2 and set a temporary reservation for ZetaCorp pool (min_reserved=1). Done — provisioning started (cloud-request id: cr-4491).
Priya (support): customer confirmed they're ok with temporary cost bump. They've also shared traces showing auth handshake took <50ms and errors were all 504 timeouts at client side.
Noah (eng-runtime): after deploying jittered backoff to staging canary, ran repro: p95 dropped to 650-800ms, p99 to ~1.7s. Cold GPU warmup still exists but the tail reduced significantly due to staggered attach.
Kevin (oncall): good. Can we also pre-warm model artifacts in image so runtime load-model time reduces? That is longer-term.
Noah (eng-runtime): roadmap item: bake model weights into warmup snapshot (artifact cache) to reduce `load-model` from 4-8s -> ~500-800ms. Needs infra work (artifact size + cache eviction policy).
Olivia (eng-sre): short-term additional mitigations: a) enable KV-prefix caching for repeated short prompts to reduce compute on attach, b) allow automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant when latency > threshold. Both doable but require product sign-off.
maria (product): sign-off for fallback to quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes. Add opt-out flag for customers who need exact model fidelity.
Priya (support): communicated to customer: applied min_reserved=1, tweaks rolling, runtime backoff patch in staging, will schedule prod roll after canary. ZetaCorp will monitor for next 24h and report.
Kevin (oncall): follow-ups: - Olivia to confirm cloud instance bootstrap telemetry (expected 6-9s) and file bug if longer. - Noah to PR backoff + handshake patch and create rollout plan (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). - Maria to draft customer communication about tradeoffs/cost. - Priya to collect post-change traces.
Olivia (eng-sre): filed infra ticket INFRA-7234 to investigate image boot variability and to add metrics: `instance_boot_ms`, `attach_handshake_ms`, `model_load_ms`.
Noah (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/482 (wip). Tests passing in CI. Will schedule canary deploy Tue 02:00 UTC.
Priya (support): customer replied: initial improvement seen — burst p95 down to ~900ms. They will keep monitoring. Thanks team :tada:
Kevin (oncall): great job. Leaving this thread open until 24h post-prod roll. Marking as action-required for listed owners.
Olivia (eng-sre): adding one extra note — we should add a default `warmup_policy` on new Dedicated pools for PLG customers to avoid too many zero-min pools by default. I'll open a product/ops RFC.
Priya (support): noted, closing loop when customer OK.
<sre-bot>: Reminder: owners assigned: Olivia, Noah, Maria. SLA review scheduled in 48h.
